raw_segments.text: but visiting to display finery, card-playing, and balls, not to mention the idle bustle
of mourning trifling, draw women from their duty, to render them insignificant, to render
them pleasing, according to the present acceptation of the word, to every man but their husband.
For a round of pleasures in which the affections are not exercised cannot be said to improve
the understanding, though it be erroneously called seeing the world. Yet the heart is
rendered cold and averse to duty by such a senseless intercourse which becomes necessary
from habit, even when it has ceased to amuse.
